summary: David Seyfort Ruegg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the Sorbonne and EPHE under Filliozat, Renou, Lalou, and Stein. He held chairs at Leiden (1966–1972), Washington (1972–1984), Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1983–1996).

David Shea worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Trinity College Dublin in 1793 and served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at East India Company College until 1836.

David Sneath is an Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge by 1991, held a fellowship at Oxford, and served as Director at Cambridge until 2009.

David Snellgrove was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Southampton and Cambridge under D. R. Shackleton Bailey, H. W. Bailey, Walter Simon, and Giuseppe Tucci. He was a professor at SOAS, University of London, from 1950 to 1982.
David Steindl-Rast is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna between approximately 1945 and 1952.

David Tracy worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University, then taught at Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and the University of Chicago (1969–2006).

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale, he served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1972–2000) and taught at Soka University of America (~2001–2004).

David W. Tien works in sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Toronto, McGill University, and the University of Michigan (PhD attested 2009), studying under Julia Ching, Robert H. Sharf, and James Robson.
David Webster is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

David White is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago. He has held posts at the University of Virginia and the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2005).

Davoud Monchi-Zadeh was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Walther Wüst, later holding posts at Munich (~1947–1951), Alexandria (~1951–1953), and Uppsala (~1954–1979).

Dawa Norbu was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Delhi, St. Stephen's College, and UC Berkeley. He taught at several institutions in San Francisco before serving as professor of Central Asian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2004).

Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobzang Trinle, held a post at Tibet University, and is attested at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as a Guest Lecturer cum Pharmacologist.

Daya Krishna was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as professor of philosophy and Ex-Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1969–1984) and chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (~1990–1993).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Oriental College and University of the Punjab. He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1931–1935) and Director of Archaeology for Jaipur (1935).

Dayong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, where he taught in 1923, and studied under Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Puren Bai, and Dorje Geshe.

Debala Mitra was an archaeologist and scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded and directed the Central Institute of Indian Languages (~1969–1989) and served as chairman of the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata, and served as a visiting professor at the University of Calcutta.
Deborah Carlson is a history and archaeology scholar who held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology (both attested 2015).
